findings.claim: Item 84 repeats the paper's claim that, over Z_p[√−p], every ordinary quadratic point of 𝒦̄' (𝒦̄ for odd k) is formally Q − u(√−p)² with u a unit, so that one blow-up gives a semistable model. That is false whenever p divides a (odd k) or b (even k). The constant term of g^{⊞k} at the point indexed by a is c = 2ap, with v_p(c) = 1 + v_p(a). By the formal Morse lemma the equation is Q(z) = −c, i.e. Q − u(√−p)^{2e} with e = 1 + v_p(a). Such points exist if and only if p² ≤ k (odd k), or 2p² ≤ k (even k, b = 2p). Counterexample: k = 9, p = 3, a = 3. The point y = (1,…,1) has local equation 18 + Σ_{i≤9} z_i² + (higher order) = 0, and 18 = 2·(√−3)^4. The Tjurina length of O[[z]]/(f, ∂f) is v_{√−3}(18) = 4, not 2, so it is not of the form Q − u(√−3)². After one blow-up the chart z = √−3·z' gives Q(z') = u(√−3)², which is still singular, and the special fibre contains the quadric cone Q(z') = 0, so it is not semistable. The same happens for k = 18, p = 3, b = 6 (c = 36). The proof of Proposition 5.23 (semistability over Q_p(√−p), and the inclusion (5.24) through Mieda's β) and hence of Corollary 5.27 is therefore incomplete for p² ≤ k (odd k) and 2p² ≤ k (even k). The statements are recovered for those p by Remark 5.41 (potential automorphy), and plausibly by iterated blow-ups. The main theorems only use p > k, where 𝒦̄' is smooth.

(1) Item 59 bundles Remark 5.41, which is about the Kloosterman system: {r_{k,ℓ}} is strictly compatible, r_{k,p} is semistable or crystalline, and M_k(p;T) satisfies Newton above Hodge. That remark uses r_{k,ℓ}, M_k(p;T) and the Hodge numbers of H¹_{dR,mid}(G_m, Sym^k Kl₂), so a general ML.2 node would have to import the Kloosterman roadmap, which itself imports ML.2. (2) Item 58's note says ML.2 is 'the potential-automorphy assembly of the ten-author CM programme, a different theorem', and the route reason says 'nothing else in the atlas plans them'. The ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions packet, however, plans ML.2 from BLGGT. It has nodes for Theorem 5.4.1/Corollary 5.4.2 (potential automorphy of totally odd, polarized, regular and irreducible weakly compatible systems over totally real fields) and for Corollary 5.4.3 (meromorphic continuation, strict purity and Λ(ıℛ,s) = ε(ıℛ,s)Λ(ıℛ^∨,1−s)). Patrikis–Taylor's Theorem A and Corollary 2.2(ii) replace irreducibility by purity, so item 59's Corollary 5.39 part partly duplicates the BLGGT node. Also: Item 59 says potential automorphy makes r_{k,p} 'semistable over Q_p for even k' for every p. The paper's argument is that ρ_{k,ℓ}(I_L) = {1} 'see Section 5.3.1'. For even k, §5.3.1 proves that inertia acts trivially on the Weil–Deligne representation only for 2 < p < ∞. At p = 2 the inertia action is unknown: Remark 5.37 lists trivial inertia only as 'one possible structure fitting these data'. So semistability of r_{k,2} over Q_2 for even k is not established. The paper itself then restricts the Newton–Hodge consequence to p ≠ 2 for even k. This is an overstatement in Remark 5.41 that the sourceIssues miss.

(see Section 5.3.1).' p. 55: 'We now suppose that k is even ... findings.claim: Five prerequisite records cite works that are not the paper's references, and two works are listed twice. (3) cites Sabbah, J. reine angew. Math. 621 (2008), arXiv:math/0508551, i.e. Part I. The paper's irregular Hodge filtration is '[50, §6]', which is Part II (Adv. Stud. Pure Math. 59, 2010). (4) gives Yu's paper as Manuscripta Math. 137 (2012); the reference is 144 (2014), as record 29 correctly says. (5) cites Adolphson–Sperber, Amer. J. Math. 109 (1987); the paper uses [2], 'On twisted de Rham cohomology', Nagoya Math. J. 146 (1997), Th. 1.4, for the Newton filtration. (14) cites two Haessig papers in Int. J. Number Theory; the paper's [25] is Math. Ann. 369 (2017), 17–47 and [26] is arXiv:2012.00570. (15) cites Broadhurst–Roberts, 'Quadratic relations between Feynman integrals'; the paper cites Broadhurst, Commun. Number Theory Phys. 10 (2016), 527–569 ([5], Eq. (128)) and the 2017 slides of Broadhurst [6] and Roberts [47]. Katz 1988 appears in both record 7 and record 25, and Yu 2014 in both record 4 and record 29. Record 2 (Kontsevich–Soibelman, '§5') omits §4 and Prop. 4.3, where EMHS and its weights are defined. Also: Prerequisite 4 cites Adolphson–Sperber, 'Twisted Kloosterman sums and p-adic Bessel functions II: Newton polygons and analytic continuation', Amer. J. Math. 109 (1987). The paper's Adolphson–Sperber reference is a different work: [2] 'On twisted de Rham cohomology', Nagoya Math. J. 146 (1997), 55–81. Item 64 and §4.3.1 cite 'Th. 1.4' of [2], the Newton-filtration description of the irregular Hodge filtration. So the prerequisite sends a worker to a paper that is not the source of the theorem used in the odd-k case of Theorem 1.8. Also: The Adolphson–Sperber prerequisite cites the wrong paper. The paper cites only [2], A. Adolphson and S. Sperber, 'On twisted de Rham cohomology', Nagoya Math. J. 146 (1997), 55–81, and its Th. 1.4 is the input of §4.3.1 that item 64 records. The prerequisite instead cites 'Twisted Kloosterman sums and p-adic Bessel functions II: Newton polygons and analytic continuation', Amer. J. Math. 109 (1987), which the paper never cites. Its stated 'why' ('The Newton-polyhedron filtration on the twisted de Rham complex of a Laurent polynomial on a torus') describes the 1997 paper. A later batch built from this list would add the wrong source. Also: Two more prerequisites for the irregular Hodge filtration of §4 are mis-cited. Prerequisite 2 cites Sabbah's 'Fourier–Laplace transform of a variation of polarized complex Hodge structure' (J. reine angew. Math., 2008; arXiv:math/0508551) for the construction of the irregular Hodge filtration in §6. The paper's [50] is the sequel, '..., II' (Adv. Stud. Pure Math. 59, 2010, 289–347), and the filtration is constructed in [50, §6]. Prerequisite 3 gives Yu's paper as Manuscripta Math. 137 (2012). The paper's [63] is Manuscripta Math. 144 (2014), 99–133, which prerequisite 29 cites correctly, so Yu is listed twice. Also: Several prerequisite entries do not match the paper's references. (1) Haessig: the entry names 'L-functions of symmetric powers of the generalized Airy family of exponential sums' and 'Meromorphy of the rank one unit root L-function revisited' (Int. J. Number Theory 2017, 2020) with link arXiv:1607.06821. That arXiv number is a physics paper (Arkani-Hamed et al., 'Nnaturalness', PRL 117 (2016)). The paper cites [25] and [26] instead. (2) Sabbah: the entry cites Part I (J. reine angew. Math. 621 (2008), arXiv:math/0508551, whose abstract concerns twistor structures) with '§6'. The irregular Hodge filtration F_Del of [50, §6.b] and Th. 6.1 are in Part II (Adv. Stud. Pure Math. 59 (2010), arXiv:0804.4328). (3) The ESY entry dates Yu's paper 'Manuscripta Math. 137 (2012)'; it is 144 (2014), as another entry correctly says. (4) Adolphson–Sperber: the entry cites 'Twisted Kloosterman sums and p-adic Bessel functions II', Amer. J. Math. 109 (1987); the paper cites [2] 'On twisted de Rham cohomology', Nagoya Math. J. 146 (1997). (5) Broadhurst–Roberts: the entry links 'Quadratic relations between Feynman integrals' (PoS 2018), which the paper does not cite. The conjectures come from [5], [6] and [47].

findings.claim: Proposition 2.7, that the symmetric powers are irreducible, uses two inputs. The first is Katz's computation of the differential Galois group, which is item 67. The second is the representation-theoretic fact that every symmetric power of the standard representation of SL_N(C) and of Sp_N(C) is irreducible (Fulton–Harris §15.3 and §17.3). Proposition 2.7 is on the main chain: it gives H⁰_dR = 0 and the concentration in degree one (Proposition 2.13), the irreducibility of M̃ (Lemma 2.24), and in §3.2.1 the concentration of the ℓ-adic cohomology in degree one. findings.claim: The paper's paraphrase of Mochizuki's definition, which item 72 copies, cannot be right as printed, and sourceIssues does not record it. (a) The multi-index is written e ∈ Z^r_{>0} with r undefined; it must be e ∈ Z^a_{>0} (one exponent per ξ_i). (b) The normal form is required 'around each point of X'. At a point of U this forces f to be 1/ξ^∅ = 1 or a coordinate ζ_1, i.e. f has no critical point. But g^{⊞k} has the critical points y = (ε_1,...,ε_k), ε_i = ±1, in G_m^k, and for even k, f-tilde_k = t g^{⊞k} has the critical curves {(t, ε): Σε_i = 0} in G_m^{k+1}. So by the printed definition neither X nor X-tilde would be non-degenerate, contrary to p. 36. (c) Along the boundary component 0 × X, where t = 0, f-tilde_k = t·g^{⊞k} is holomorphic and vanishes. Neither 1/ξ^e nor ζ_1/ξ^e with e > 0 has that form (ζ_1 = f·ξ^e would vanish on D, so it could not be a coordinate independent of ξ). The normal form has to be imposed only near the pole divisor, with no condition where f is holomorphic.
findings.evidence: p. 35, §4.3.2: 'After Mochizuki [43, Def. 2.6], we call a smooth compactification X of U non-degenerate along D if the boundary D = X ∖ U is a strict normal crossing divisor and f extends to a rational morphism f: X ⇢ P1 such that, locally for the analytic topology around each point of X, there is a coordinate system {ξ1, . . . , ξa, η1, . . . , ηb, ζ1, . . . , ζc} and a multi-index e ∈ Z^r_{>0} satisfying D = (ξη), f = 1/ξ^e or ζ1/ξ^e.' p. 36: 'The toric variety X provides an example of a non-degenerate compactification of (G^k_m, g^⊞k)'; '... e X is a non-degenerate compactification of the pair (G^{k+1}_m, f̃k)'. findings.claim: Three notes misdescribe the paper. Item 35's note speaks of 'clause (4) … self-duality and clause (5) … Fourier transform', but Proposition 2.4 has only clauses (1)–(4): duality is (3) and the Fourier description is (4). The same note says the proof works by 'transposing Deligne's ℓ-adic arguments', whereas the paper says it uses the recursion instead. Item 36's note says irreducibility 'is what makes the intermediate extension at the origin equal to the minimal extension'. That is meaningless, since the two are equal by definition. The actual uses are H⁰_dR = 0 (Proposition 2.13) and the irreducibility of M̃ (Lemma 2.24). Item 42's note puts the singular points of 𝒦 at 'the points whose coordinates are (n+1)-st roots of unity summing to zero'. Remark 3.10 requires more: the coordinates are constant inside each block, y_{ji} = ζ_j, and Σ_j ζ_j = 0. The note's version admits smooth points.
findings.evidence: p. 11: 'The arguments of [9, Th. 7.4 & 7.8] can readily be transposed … Instead, we give a proof based on the following recursive description.' p. 22, Remark 3.10: 'its Q̄-singular points being those with coordinates y_{ji} = ζ_j for all 1 ⩽ j ⩽ k and 1 ⩽ i ⩽ n, where ζ_j ∈ µ_{n+1} are roots of unity satisfying Σ_{j=1}^k ζ_j = 0'. Counterexample to item 42's wording: n = 2, k = 3, ω a primitive cube root of 1, y = ((1, ω), (ω², 1), (ω, ω²)). All six coordinates are cube roots of unity with sum 2(1 + ω + ω²) = 0. Each block has g = 1 + ω + ω² = 0, so y ∈ 𝒦. But ∂g^{⊞3}/∂y_{11} = 1 − 1/(y_{11}²y_{12}) = 1 − ω² ≠ 0, so y is a smooth point.
findings.fix: Item 35 note: 'clause (3) gives the self-duality of the symmetric powers and clause (4) puts the computation inside the theory of mixed Hodge modules; the proof is by the recursion Kl_{n+2} ≅ ℱ inv^+Kl_{n+1} of Lemma 2.5 rather than by transposing Deligne'. Item 36 note: 'Used for H⁰_dR(G_m, Sym^k Kl_{n+1}) = 0 (Proposition 2.13) and the irreducibility of M̃ (Lemma 2.24).' Item 42 note: 'at the points with y_{ji} = ζ_j for all i, where ζ_j ∈ µ_{n+1} and Σ_j ζ_j = 0'.

findings.claim: The report sets aside three real (minor) slips that should be sourceIssues. (a) Remark 5.28 says the even-k Hodge polygons of H¹_{dR,c} lie 'strictly above' the polygon with vertices n(n−1). For k = 6 the vertices are (1,0), (2,2), (3,7) against (1,0), (2,2), (3,6), so they coincide up to n = 2. In general they coincide up to n = ⌊(k−1)/4⌋ + 1, plus one more vertex when 4 | k. (b) §5.3.1 calls det(ρ) 'the non-trivial character' of Q_p(√±k!!), which can be trivial locally. (c) The proof of Corollary 5.27 'puts the trivial factor back'. For even k and p ≤ k/2, H¹_{rig,c} also contains the ⌊k/2p⌋ further factors of R_k(p;T) of slope k/2, and is shorter than H¹_{dR,c}. The statement still holds: slopes k/2 inserted in place of the lost middle slopes keep the Newton polygon above the Hodge polygon, by the symmetry of the middle slopes about (k+1)/2. But the printed proof does not say so.
